Definition: A metric chosen because it reflects how well the business (or a specific part of it) is performing against its goals.
A reference point -- often an industry average or a past result -- used to judge whether a current number is good or not.
The share of time a system or piece of equipment was available and working.
The level of performance the business aims to reach for a measure in a given period.
A number that is tracked to show how something is performing, such as sales, defects or hours worked.

Also known as: OKR; Objective and Key Result; KR
Definition: A measurable outcome used to show whether an objective has been reached.

Also known as: Base Period; Starting Point; Reference Value
Definition: The starting value that later results are compared with to see whether things have improved.
A set value which, when crossed, triggers an action or changes a status, for example from green to amber.

Also known as: Allowed Variation; Acceptable Range; Tolerance Band
Definition: The amount by which a result may differ from the target before it is treated as a problem.

Also known as: RAG Status; Traffic Light; Health Status
Definition: A simple label, often green, amber or red, showing how a measure is doing against its target.

Also known as: Trend Line; Direction of Travel; Movement
Definition: The general direction in which a measure is moving over time, such as up, down or flat.

Also known as: Moving Average; Running Average; Rolling Mean
Definition: The average of the latest few periods, recalculated each period, which smooths out short-term ups and downs.

Also known as: Rolling Total; Running Total; Cumulative Total
Definition: The sum of the values over the latest few periods, or from the start up to now, updated each period.

Also known as: Previous Year; Last Year; PY; LY
Definition: The same measure for the previous year, used for comparison.
The same measure for the period just before the one being shown, such as last month.

Also known as: SPLY; Same Period Prior Year; Like for Like Period
Definition: The same measure for the same dates a year earlier, which avoids the effect of seasons.
The change in a measure compared with the previous month.
The change in a measure compared with the previous quarter.
The change in a measure compared with the previous week.

Also known as: Percent Change; Change Percentage; Growth Percentage
Definition: The change between two values shown as a percentage of the earlier one.
The plain difference between two values, not shown as a percentage.

Also known as: Gap to Target; Target Variance; Difference to Target
Definition: How far the actual result is above or below the target.

Also known as: Budget Variance; Gap to Budget; Over or Under Budget
Definition: How far the actual result is above or below the budget.

Also known as: Year on Year Difference; Gap to Last Year
Definition: How far the actual result is above or below the same period of the previous year.

Also known as: Annualised Run Rate; Current Run Rate
Definition: The expected yearly total if the current level of results carried on for the whole year.
The sum of all the values being shown. It is the simplest way to combine many values into one.
The sum of the values divided by how many there are.
The middle value when all the values are put in order, which is less affected by extreme values than the average.
The smallest value in a set. It shows the lowest level reached.
The largest value in a set. It shows the highest level reached.

Also known as: Number of; Record Count; Row Count
Definition: The number of items or records, such as orders, people or events.

Also known as: Unique Count; Number of Unique; Count of Unique
Definition: The number of different values, with repeats counted once, for example the number of different customers.

Also known as: Rate per Hour; Rate per Day
Definition: An amount measured against a unit of time or volume, such as per hour or per thousand.

Also known as: Index Value; Indexed Value; Index Score
Definition: A number that shows a value relative to a base, normally set at 100.

Also known as: Rating Score; Composite Score; Overall Score
Definition: A single number, often built from several measures, that sums up how something is doing.
An average in which some values count for more than others, according to their size or importance.

Also known as: Percent of Total; Contribution; Proportion of Total
Definition: A part shown as a percentage of the total of all the parts.
The money left from sales after the variable costs have been taken off, which goes towards covering fixed costs and profit.
The idea that a small number of causes, often about 20%, produce most of the effects, often about 80%.
A list of the best or biggest items by a measure, such as the top 10 customers by sales.
The position of an item when all items are put in order by a measure.
The value below which a given share of the observations fall, for example the 90th percentile.
A value that is far away from the normal pattern and may need to be checked.

Also known as: Seasonal Pattern; Seasonal Index; Seasonal Effect
Definition: A pattern that repeats at the same time each year, such as higher sales before a holiday.
A measure that tends to change before the result it influences, so it gives an early warning.
A measure that shows results after they have happened, such as profit or sales.
The span of time that a report covers, such as a month or quarter.
The twelve-month period used by a business for its accounts, which may not start in January.
The twelve months from 1 January to 31 December.

Also known as: Data Refresh Date; Last Updated; As of Date
Definition: The date and time when the data in the report was last updated.

Also known as: Data Accuracy; Data Completeness; Data Integrity
Definition: How accurate, complete and consistent the data is for the use it is put to.

Also known as: Source System; Source of Data; Data Origin
Definition: The system or file that the data in a report comes from.
A way of splitting a measure into groups, such as by region, product or month.
A control on a report that lets people choose which part of the data they want to see.

Also known as: Drill Down; Drill-Through Page; Detail Page
Definition: Going from a summary figure to the page or table that shows the detail behind it.
Extra information that appears when the pointer is placed over a part of a chart.
A saved view of a report page, with its filters and settings, that can be returned to.
The share of cases where rules, standards or policies were followed.

Also known as: Risk Rating; Risk Level; Risk Index
Definition: A score showing how likely and how serious a risk is. A higher score means more risk.
An important point in a project, such as the end of a stage, used to track progress.
The share of items finished or delivered by the date promised.
How much of a task or project is done, shown as a percentage of the whole.

Also known as: Past Due; Late Items; Delayed Items
Definition: The number of items that have passed their due date without being completed.

Also known as: Work in Queue; Queue Length; Pending Items
Definition: The number of items waiting to be dealt with.

Also known as: TAT; Processing Time; Time to Complete
Definition: The time taken from receiving a request to completing it.

Also known as: Total Elapsed Time; Elapsed Time; End to End Time
Definition: The total time an item takes to pass through a process from start to finish.
The share of items that came back after being sent out.
The share of results that were correct. It is shown as a percentage of all results checked.
The number of mistakes found in a period.
